previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure (EF 35%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for chest pain, shortness of breath, and leg swelling over two days. He reported a heavy central chest pressure worsened by breathing and coughing, along with a dry cough and orthopnea. Initial evaluation showed elevated BNP (3969), mild pulmonary congestion on chest X-ray, and stable renal function. He was treated with furosemide for volume overload, with improvement in symptoms and respiratory status. His ICD was checked and functioning properly, with no shocks but recorded NSVT. H. pylori testing was negative. He was discharged home with continued diuretic therapy, instructions to monitor weight, avoid salt, and follow up with his cardiologist and primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ M with h/o sCHF, HTN, HLD, CAD, and multiple admissions for 
CHF exacerbations (most recent D/C 1 week ago) presents with 
acute weight gain concerning for CHF exacerbation.

ACTIVE DIAGNOSES

#  ACUTE ON CHRONIC SYSTOLIC HEART FAILURE:  Pt has h/o severe 
ischemic disease with EF 35-40% in ___ (as low as 20% on 
prior echo).  Suspect excessive fluids as possible explanation 
for repeat exacerbation.  Also, it appears pt has been taking 
torsemide at home in divided doses through the day.  ICD was 
interrogated and showed no explanation for exacerbation.

Diuresis was undertaken with Lasix 80mg IV boluses and then pt 
transitioned to torsemide 80mg PO daily.  Home spironolactone 
was continued.  Electrolytes were monitored and repleted.  2gm 
sodium diet, strict I/O, daily weights, and fluid restriction 
(2L, then changed to 1.5L) were enacted.  Nutrition consult was 
obtained to counsel pt on importance of heart-healthy diet.  Dry 
weight last admission was estimated at 137.8kg.  Pt weighed 
138.9kg on day of dishcarge.  Counseled pt on importance of 
taking full dose of torsemide at single time.  He should follow 
closely with Cardiology as outpatient.

#  SOB:  Ddx includes CHF exacerbation vs pulmonary HTN vs COPD. 
 Pt had persistent SOB despite diuresis, and SOB persisted 
despite minimal rales at the very bases of lungs.  He breathed 
stably on room air and maintained SpO2 92-100% with ambulation.  
He was encouraged to follow-up with his PCP for outpatient 
pulmonary function tests.

#  CAD: known 60% mid LAD occlusion.  Trops here 0.04-0.05; have 
been elevated on prior admissions as well.  ___ be related to 
demand ischemia in setting of CHF, with decreased clearance of 
trop due to CKD.  Pt had increased severity of baseline CP one 
night and ECG was stable compared to prior.  Repeat trop was 
also stable.  Continued home isosorbide mononitrate, statin, 
beta-blocker and aspirin.  Temporarily DCed losartan due to 
slight increase in Cr but restarted on day of discharge.

#  CKD:  likely secondary to chronic hypoperfusive state and 
longstanding hypertensive disease, as well as DM. Cr fluctuated 
within pt's normal range this admission.  Losartan was 
temporarily held but restarted on day of discharge.  
Electrolytes were checked BID while actively diuresing.
 
CHRONIC DIAGNOSES

#DM: Continued home dose of 40 units glargine.  Pt was also 
placed on SSI.

#OSA:  Pt has h/o OSA and had multiple desaturations on 
telemetry.  Trialed CPAP mask on night prior to discharge but 
was unable to tolerate.  Encouraged pt to d/w PCP ___: outpatient 
sleep study.

#Tachy-Brady:  has dual chamber ICD/pacer in place.  ICD was 
interrogated and showed:

""- Normal device function
- No prolonged episodes of tachycardia since last interrogation
- No pace-terminated or shock terminated episodes 
- No episodes of VF, <0.1 hr/day in AF/AT
- No findings on device interrogation to explain acute heart
failure exacerbation."
